title: OTel collector test fixture: wait for the health_check endpoint before yielding, and always stop the container in finally
answers: Why does the OpenTelemetry collector test fixture flake or sleep for five seconds before tracing tests run?
How do I add a new tracing test that needs the OTLP collector to be ready, and how is it torn down?
Where is the collector readiness check and shutdown handled for the OTLP export tests?
body:
Path: tests/tracing/conftest.py:otel_collector is the pytest fixture that starts a Docker OpenTelemetry collector for OTLP trace export tests (single export and dual MLflow+OTel export in tests/tracing/utils/test_otlp.py). It launches `docker run` via subprocess.Popen and yields (log_path, otlp_port) to consumers.
Rule: readiness is decided by polling the collector's health_check extension over HTTP (requests.get on 127.0.0.1:<health_port>/ until status 200, 10 second deadline, 0.1s interval), not by a fixed time.sleep. Inside the readiness loop, if process.poll() shows the container already exited, the fixture raises RuntimeError with the captured log file contents; on deadline it raises TimeoutError with the logs. Termination (terminate, wait 5s, then kill) lives in a finally block around the yield so readiness failures also stop the container.
Symptom: tests slept a fixed five seconds and could start sending spans before the collector listened, or the collector kept running after a failed startup. Early exits gave no diagnostic output.
Constraints: applies to the Docker-based collector fixture only; if you add another external process fixture, copy the poll-then-yield-then-finally shape rather than sleeping. Requires the health_check extension to be enabled in the collector config (service.extensions).
applies: Test fixtures in tests/tracing that start the OpenTelemetry collector container.
says: Tracing export test suite flakes intermittently because the background collector takes too long starting up.
Spans sent during automated tracing tests are lost before the trace receiver starts listening.
Container processes left behind after failed tracing test runs keep holding local ports open.
Show diagnostic logs immediately when background trace collector fails during local test execution.
Stop relying on arbitrary sleep delays before running automated trace export validation suites.
search: In tests/tracing/conftest.py:otel_collector, the Docker OpenTelemetry collector fixture for OTLP trace export tests in tests/tracing/utils/test_otlp.py polls the HTTP health_check extension endpoint until status 200 rather than using time.sleep. If process.poll() indicates an early exit or the ten-second deadline expires, the fixture raises RuntimeError or TimeoutError with log contents, and container termination is guaranteed in a finally block. This applies specifically to the Docker-based collector fixture and requires service.extensions to enable health_check.
